source_text: V. Martianus ait: Omnium trade mihi nomina. respondit Achatius: Nomina eorum caelesti libro et divinis paginis sunt annotata. quomodo ergo oculi mortales aspicient quod immortalis virtus dei et invisibilis annotavit? Martianus ait: Ubi sunt magi, socii artis tuae vel doctores huius artificiosae fallaciae? respondit Achatius: Nos omnia meruimus a deo et meremur, sectam vero magicae artis horremus. Martianus ait: Ideo magi estis quia novum nescio quod genus religionis inducitis. respondit Achatius: Illos destruimus quos vos prius facitis et a vobis factos ipsi timetis. deficient enim vobis dii, si artifex saxo, aut saxum non abundaret artifici. timemus enim nos illum, non quem fabricamus, sed a quo fabricati sumus; qui nos creavit ut dominus, amavit ut pater, et aeternae morti, quasi bonus patronus, eripuit.
thought_title: Refusing to give names and rejecting the sorcery charge
orientation: Martianus interrogates Achatius, demanding the names of the others and accusing Christians of sorcery for introducing a new religion.
pass_a_gloss: Martianus said: Hand over to me the names of all. Achatius answered: Their names have been written down in a heavenly book and in divine pages. How therefore will mortal eyes look upon what the immortal and invisible power of God has written down? Martianus said: Where are the sorcerers, the companions of your craft or the teachers of this cunning deception? Achatius answered: We have received all things from God and do receive them, but we shudder at the sect of the magical art. Martianus said: You are sorcerers for this reason, because you introduce some new unknown kind of religion. Achatius answered: We destroy those gods whom you first make and, once made by you, you yourselves fear. For gods will fail you, if the craftsman should lack stone, or stone should not be abundant for the craftsman. For we fear him, not whom we fashion, but by whom we have been fashioned; who created us as lord, loved us as father, and, as a good patron, snatched us from eternal death.

pass_b_english: Martianus said, "Give me the names of them all." Achatius answered, "Their names are written in the heavenly book, on the pages of God. How then could mortal eyes see what the immortal and invisible power of God has written?"

Martianus said, "Where are the sorcerers, the partners in your craft or the teachers of this cunning deception?" Achatius answered, "We have received everything from God, and we still receive it. But we dread the school of the magical art." Martianus said, "You are sorcerers because you are bringing in some new kind of religion or other."

Achatius answered, "We destroy the ones you first make yourselves, and then fear once you have made them. Your gods will run out if the craftsman runs short of stone, or the stone finds no craftsman. For we fear him, not one we make, but one by whom we were made. As Lord he created us, as Father he loved us, and like a good patron he snatched us from eternal death."
